title: Shader Energy Transfer Studio
description: An avocado and a silk pouf sit on a reflective plane, connected by a visible energy beam. The user manipulates custom shader parameters on each object — glow intensity, fresnel power, chromatic shift, and dissolve threshold — while a conservation law ensures the total shader energy budget across both objects remains constant. Adjusting one object's shader automatically redistributes energy to the other, with full undo/redo support.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that loads Avocado.glb and SpecularSilkPouf.glb via GLTFLoader. Place the avocado on the left and the pouf on the right on a reflective MeshStandardMaterial ground plane. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,1.5,3) looking at origin with OrbitControls. Add an HDR-style lighting rig: one DirectionalLight, one HemisphereLight, and one PointLight between the objects.

Replace each model's materials with ShaderMaterial using custom vertex/fragment shaders. Each object's shader must support four uniform parameters: glowIntensity (0-1), fresnelPower (0.5-5), chromaticShift (0-0.1 UV offset for RGB channel separation), and dissolveThreshold (0-1 using a noise pattern to discard fragments). The shaders should sample the original texture via a uniform sampler2D extracted from the loaded GLTF material.

Implement a CONSERVATION LAW: define a global energy budget of 4.0. The sum of all 8 parameters (4 per object) must always equal 4.0. When the user adjusts any slider, proportionally scale the OTHER object's corresponding parameter to maintain the total. Display the current energy sum in a HUD overlay.

Create an HTML panel with 8 labeled range sliders (4 per object, color-coded blue for avocado, pink for pouf). Add a visible energy beam between objects using a custom ShaderMaterial cylinder whose color and opacity reflect the current energy distribution ratio.

Implement an undo/redo system: store snapshots of all 8 parameter values on each slider change in a history stack (max 50 entries). Add Undo (Ctrl+Z) and Redo (Ctrl+Y) buttons and keyboard shortcuts. Each undo/redo restores all 8 uniforms and updates sliders and the beam simultaneously.

Add a Reset button that sets all parameters to 0.5 (totaling 4.0). The dissolve shader should use a smooth noise function (simplex or value noise in GLSL) so fragments fade organically. Fresnel should highlight edges with an emissive color that shifts based on chromaticShift. Ensure the scene runs at 60fps with requestAnimationFrame and all uniforms update in the render loop.
